clinicalPearls: The defining combination is congenital cataracts, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, skeletal (mitochondrial) myopathy and exercise intolerance with lactic acidosis
It is an autosomal recessive nuclear disorder caused by mutations in AGK, encoding acylglycerol kinase, a mitochondrial protein involved in lipid metabolism and mitochondrial protein import
Congenital or early cataracts are a consistent and often presenting feature that should prompt cardiac evaluation
Lactate rises markedly with exertion despite normal cognition, and the myopathy causes hypotonia and fatigue
The hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the principal determinant of prognosis and can cause heart failure or arrhythmia
A severe neonatal form presents early with profound cardiomyopathy and lactic acidosis, while a milder form allows survival into adulthood
Care is supportive with cataract surgery, cardiac management and avoidance of mitochondrial toxins; intellect is typically preserved
reference.pathophysiology: Sengers syndrome is caused by recessive loss-of-function mutations in AGK, which encodes acylglycerol kinase. This mitochondrial enzyme phosphorylates monoacylglycerol and diacylglycerol and also functions as a component of the TIM22 carrier import machinery that inserts certain proteins, including the adenine nucleotide translocator, into the inner mitochondrial membrane. Loss of AGK disturbs mitochondrial membrane lipid composition and impairs import of key carriers, secondarily compromising oxidative phosphorylation and ATP export. Tissues with high and sustained energy demand, notably cardiac and skeletal muscle, and the metabolically specialised lens are preferentially affected, giving the cardiomyopathy, myopathy and cataracts.
additionalDifferentials: Other mitochondrial cardiomyopathies and Barth syndrome
Infantile Pompe disease and other metabolic cardiomyopathies
Sarcomeric (genetic) hypertrophic cardiomyopathy without metabolic features
Congenital cataract syndromes of other cause
Other combined oxidative phosphorylation deficiency disorders
additionalInvestigations: Echocardiography and ECG to detect and monitor hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia
Ophthalmological examination for congenital or early cataract
Skeletal muscle biopsy for histology and respiratory-chain enzymology
Creatine kinase and assessment of the myopathy
redFlags: Decompensated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or heart failure
Severe neonatal lactic acidosis with cardiorespiratory compromise
Rapid clinical deterioration during intercurrent illness or metabolic stress
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is bimodal: the severe neonatal form usually causes death in infancy from cardiomyopathy and lactic acidosis, whereas the milder form permits survival into adulthood with cataract, myopathy and manageable cardiac disease, cardiac status being the main prognostic factor.
pitfalls: Treating congenital cataracts in isolation without evaluating the heart, thereby missing the cardiomyopathy
Attributing the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy to a sarcomeric cause and overlooking a metabolic origin
Assuming cognitive impairment, when intellect is characteristically preserved
Exposing patients to mitochondrial toxins that can worsen the energy deficit
management: Provide supportive management of this AGK-related mitochondrial disorder, for which no curative therapy exists
Arrange surgical extraction of congenital cataracts to preserve vision and support development
Treat the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and any arrhythmia with heart failure and antiarrhythmic therapy, the principal determinant of prognosis
Avoid prolonged fasting and metabolic stressors, and manage exercise intolerance and lactic acidosis with graded activity and carbohydrate support
Undertake surveillance with serial echocardiography, ECG, and resting and post-exercise lactate monitoring
Coordinate multidisciplinary care across metabolic or mitochondrial medicine, cardiology, and ophthalmology
Offer genetic counselling and family screening for this autosomal recessive condition, including reproductive options
